title: Derivation of the Entropy Production Function Γ(ρ) from Grid-Mode Bose–Einstein Statistics
description: Derives the entropy production function Γ(ρ) from first principles using Bose–Einstein occupation statistics of grid modes and the von Neumann entropy functional. The work yields a saturating form Γ(ρ) = Γ0 · ρ/(ρ + ρcrit) with ρcrit emerging from the grid-mode energy scale a0, satisfying low-density linearity and high-density saturation. It also clarifies that Γ(ρ) and the gravitational response μBE(g) are distinct dynamical and static quantities, resolving potential double-counting.
author: Morten Magnusson

flow_constraint.description: EFC flow constraint where the entropy production function Γ(ρ) sources the scalar flow.

be_occupation.description: Bose–Einstein occupation number for grid modes at gravitational acceleration g with characteristic scale a0.

g_of_rho.description: Characteristic gravitational acceleration at scale r∗, defining β = 4πG_N r∗/3.

x_of_rho.description: Dimensionless energy variable controlling the BE occupation.

vn_entropy_per_mode.description: Von Neumann entropy per bosonic mode with occupation n.

entropy_marginal.description: Marginal entropy per mode for the BE-distributed grid modes; a key step in the derivation.

gamma_result.description: Derived functional form: linear at low density and saturating at high density, with an emergent critical density ρcrit set by the grid microphysics via a0.

key_results.main_finding: From BE occupation plus von Neumann entropy, Γ(ρ) takes the saturating form Γ0·ρ/(ρ+ρcrit) with ρcrit emerging from the a0 grid-mode scale, and Γ is shown to be distinct from μBE(g), resolving double-counting.

sealed_predictions.statement: In any EFC implementation using this microphysical bridge, the inferred Γ(ρ) from cosmological evolution must be linear in ρ at low densities and saturate to a constant at high densities, with the transition density correlated with the MOND scale a0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Reconstruction of Γ(ρ) from EFC-consistent simulations or observationally constrained background+perturbation evolution that demands sub/super-linear low-ρ scaling or non-saturating high-ρ behavior, or a ρcrit uncorrelated with a0.

kill_criteria: KC1: Empirical or simulation-based reconstruction of Γ(ρ) in an EFC-consistent cosmology shows no high-density saturation (Γ → const fails) at >5σ significance.

KC2: The transition (critical) density ρcrit inferred from fits is inconsistent with the a0-determined microphysical scale by more than an order of magnitude without compensating model changes; i.e., ρcrit cannot be tied to a0.

KC3: Joint fits to galactic dynamics (μBE(g)) and cosmological evolution (Γ(ρ)) require identifying μBE and Γ as the same effective quantity to succeed, indicating unresolved double-counting in contradiction with the paper’s separation.
KC4: Robust EFC simulations with the derived Γ(ρ) yield negative total entropy production (dS/dt < 0) under monotonic density decrease, violating the second law.
KC5: Observational constraints decisively rule out μBE(g) = 1/(e^{g/a0}−1) as the grid-mode response, thereby invalidating the shared statistical basis used to derive Γ(ρ).
key_result: Γ(ρ) ∝ ρ^(3/2)/(ρ+ρ_crit) from BE+vN entropy — Scenario B; double-counting resolved
